README: Captured readings of the Linux TPM surface, replayed by tpm2-linux-probe.test.ts against
classifyTpm2Linux(). Text, diffable, DST-replayable — no binary in the proof lineage.
PROVENANCE IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS NOT DECORATION. Every entry carries `provenance`, and
on the named host, and `expectedState` was written by the person who was
hand-constructed — written by an agent from the documented shapes of sysfs and tpm2-tools.
It exercises the parser and the state machine. It is NOT evidence that any
machine ever behaved this way, and it must never be cited as a TPM having
AS OF 2026-08-17 EXACTLY ONE ENTRY IS `observed`, AND IT IS THE macOS ONE — i.e. the entry
that proves only that the probe declines to answer where it cannot ask. No TPM has been
contacted by anyone in this repo. Closing that gap is workitem 081M00VN9P1087G0R000FYTTVS:
run the capture command on an x86 node, fill in `expectedState` from what the BIOS and
`tpm2_getcap` actually say, and append the entry here.
`expectedState` is deliberately the operator's reading of the machine and not the
classifier's output, so a wrong classifier is caught rather than ratified.

captures.name: macos-apple-silicon-mac-studio
captures.provenance: Otto, 2026-08-17, Darwin 25.5.0 arm64 (Mac Studio, T6020) — `ls /dev/tpm*` matched nothing and /sys does not exist on this OS at all.
captures.why: macOS has no Linux TPM interface. The honest answer is 'not asked', never 'no TPM' — even though it also happens to be true that this machine has no TPM 2.0.

captures.name: linux-x86-tpm2-present
captures.provenance: Hand-constructed by Otto from the documented shapes: drivers/char/tpm/tpm-sysfs.c exports tpm_version_major since kernel 4.19, and tpm2-tools 5.x emits properties-fixed as YAML. NO TPM WAS CONTACTED.
captures.why: The only path to `present`: a usable device node AND a positive family-2.0 reading.

captures.name: linux-x86-ftpm-disabled-in-firmware
captures.provenance: Hand-constructed by Otto. The case the work-item's title names: fTPM commonly ships disabled in BIOS. NO TPM WAS CONTACTED.
captures.why: The kernel exposes the tpm class and it enumerates no chip. That is a real enumeration returning a real negative — the ONLY path to `absent`.

captures.name: linux-tpm-driver-not-loaded
captures.provenance: Hand-constructed by Otto. A kernel with tpm_tis not loaded (or built without TPM support). NO TPM WAS CONTACTED.
captures.why: No tpm class at all, so 'no TPM installed' and 'driver not loaded' are indistinguishable. Reporting this as `absent` would be a check that did not run looking like one that ran and said no — and on an x86 node with an fTPM enabled in BIOS it would be flatly wrong.

captures.name: linux-unprivileged-caller-denied
captures.provenance: Hand-constructed by Otto. A caller outside the tss group on a host where the TPM is real. NO TPM WAS CONTACTED.
captures.why: The node exists and refuses us. A privileged caller gets a different answer, so this is never `absent`.

captures.name: linux-tpm12-chip-only
captures.provenance: Hand-constructed by Otto. An older x86 box whose chip is TPM 1.2. NO TPM WAS CONTACTED.
captures.why: /dev/tpm0 EXISTS and is a TPM 1.2 node. The old boolean probe reported this machine as TPM-2.0-available on the strength of the node alone — the same 'a thing associated with the capability is not the capability' error as the PKCS#11-driver regression. TPM 2.0 is absent here; the machine still has a TPM, and the state says so.

getcapPropertiesFixed.stderr: ERROR: Esys_GetCapability(0x9A2) - tpm:warn(2.0): the 1.2 TPM is not a 2.0 TPM

captures.name: linux-old-kernel-no-version-file-no-tools
captures.provenance: Hand-constructed by Otto. Kernel older than 4.19 (no tpm_version_major) with tpm2-tools not installed. NO TPM WAS CONTACTED.
captures.why: A node is there and nothing can say which family it is. Not `present` (that would be rounding an unconfirmed device up to a capability), not `absent` (there is plainly a TPM), not `unreadable` (nothing denied us). The fifth state exists for exactly this.

captures.name: linux-getcap-ran-but-said-nothing-about-family
captures.provenance: Hand-constructed by Otto. The #11509 trap given a body: a tool that RUNS, exits 0, and does not answer the question asked. NO TPM WAS CONTACTED.
captures.why: Exit 0 with no TPM2_PT_FAMILY_INDICATOR is silence, not a negative. A parser that read 'the property is not in the output' as 'the family is not 2.0' would be the empty-grep bug; a parser that read exit-0 as success would be the opposite one.

captures.name: linux-x86-tpm2-present-nist-curves-only
captures.provenance: Hand-constructed by Nazar from the output shape of tpm2-tools tools/tpm2_getcap.c dump_ecc_curves, which prints NAME: 0xHEX for the eight identifiers it recognises. NO TPM WAS CONTACTED.
captures.why: A TPM 2.0 that enumerated its ECC curves and reported only TCG-registered NIST curves. This is the ONLY shape that settles secp256k1 negatively, because every identifier was one the tool could name.

captures.name: linux-x86-tpm2-present-vendor-curve-unnameable
captures.provenance: Hand-constructed by Nazar from the default branch of tpm2-tools dump_ecc_curves, which prints unknownHEX: 0xHEX for an identifier it cannot name. NO TPM WAS CONTACTED.
captures.why: The same TPM plus one identifier tpm2-tools cannot name. secp256k1 has no TCG code point, so a vendor implementation would look EXACTLY like this. The curve is not excluded, and calling this absent would be the whole defect.

captures.name: linux-x86-tpm2-present-no-tpm2-tools
captures.provenance: Hand-constructed by Nazar. A real TPM 2.0 with tpm2-tools absent, so the curve question was never asked. NO TPM WAS CONTACTED.
captures.why: The vacuity guard given a body: a machine that HAS a TPM and cannot be asked about curves. Reading this as no-secp256k1 is the failure this probe exists to prevent, so this entry fails a classifier that does.

captures.name: linux-x86-tpm2-version-file-unrecognised
captures.provenance: Hand-constructed by the shadow 2026-08-21 to kill a mutant that SURVIVED tpm-shell-parity.test.ts: no committed capture held a tpm_version_major that was neither "1" nor "2", so a classifier that DEFAULTED an unrecognised value to 2.0 passed every fixture on both implementations. NO TPM WAS CONTACTED.
captures.why: A device node exists and the family indicator says something the kernel contract does not define. `unrecognised` must never round up to 2.0 -- that is the whole difference between `indeterminate` and a false `present`, and it is why parseVersionMajor has three outcomes instead of a boolean. Verified to fail both the TypeScript classifier and the bash port when either one defaults.
